newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Fruit of the Loom says committed to Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Fruit of the Loom says committed to Ireland.

text.p: U.S. textile manufacturer Fruit of the Loom Inc said it remained committed to its Irish operations and business would continue as usual.
In a statement released on Sunday, Fruit of the Loom also said it was "appalled at the media campaign which is being orchestrated against the company and its senior management".
The statement follows rumours that the group could transfer some of its manufacturing operations to a cheaper location with the loss of up to 1,000 jobs in Ireland.
Speculation about Fruit of the Loom's plans for its Irish businesses began after it issued redundancy notices to its three top Irish executives last week.

Managing director Willie McCarter, his brother and sales director John McCarter and finance director Seamus McEleney were served with redundancy notices by Fruit of the Loom which owns 100 percent of the Irish businesses.
The three managers have taken an injunction against the company in Dublin's High Court and the case is listed for hearing on August 27.

"We wish to restate that contrary to intense media speculation we are not in dispute with any of our employees in the north-west of Ireland other than with three named managers who have been given redundancy notices," Fruit of the Loom said.
"These notices have been given as part of a European reorganisation of our business whereby management responsibility is being centralised elsewhere."
It said the dispute with the three managers had no adverse effect on employment at its plants in Donegal and Londonderry.
Fruit of the Loom also said it had written to Ireland's Enterprise and Employment Minister Mary Harney to inform her that the current dispute was causing deep concern to the company.
It told her that the proceedings, which were attracting so much unwanted publicity, related only to the three individuals.
Harney, is expected to travel to Chicago to discuss the matter with Fruit of the Loom's parent company, official sources said.
The High Court case is not expected to be heard for up to two weeks and Fruit of the Loom said it would make no further comment until the case is concluded.
Fruit of the Loom employs 3,500 people in Ireland and in Northern Ireland in what is seen by the British and Irish governments as a model cross-border operation.
In 1986, it bought McCarter's Ireland interests in Derry and Donegal from the McCarter family, and Willie McCarter was appointed managing director of the Irish operations in 1987.

Media reports suggest files at the Company Records office show that Fruit of the Loom in Ireland slid into the red, recording a pre-tax loss of 13.5 million Irish pounds ($19.7 million) in 1995, down from a profit of 5.8 million in 1994.
McCarter is heavily involved in cross border relations and is chairman of the International Fund for Ireland, a multinational private fund which collects and distributes investment in Irish projects.
